previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with HLA-B27 positive ankylosing spondylitis, hypertension, asthma, obstructive sleep apnea, and anxiety, was admitted for an acute flare of chronic back and bilateral sacroiliac joint pain, worse on the left, with difficulty ambulating. He recently completed a prednisone taper but declined further steroids or biologics due to recurrent infections. Labs showed no active infection or inflammation. Pain was managed with Dilaudid and cyclobenzaprine, and a new prescription for nortriptyline was started for chronic pain. He was discharged home in stable condition after two days with instructions to follow up with rheumatology, pain management, and his PCP, continue home medications, and wean off opioids as able.
problems: Ankylosing spondylitis of unspecified sites in spine

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  INJ/ASP MAJOR JT W/FLUORO

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with sacroiliitis p/W exacerbation of L hip pain 
// Please perform L hip joint treatment under fluoro

TECHNIQUE:  The risks, benefits and alternatives were explained to the patient
and written informed consent was obtained.

A pre-procedure timeout confirmed three patient identifiers.

Under fluoroscopic guidance, an appropriate spot was marked. The area was
prepared and draped in standard sterile fashion.

3 cc 1% Lidocaine was used to achieve local anesthesia.

Under intermittent fluoroscopic guidance, a 20-gauge spinal needle was
advanced into the LEFT HIP joint.

Appropriate position was confirmed by the injection of a small amount of 
water-soluble contrast. Then, 5 cc of a solution of  0.25% Marcaineand  80 mg
Kenalog was injected into the joint.

The needle was removed, hemostasis achieved, and a sterile bandage applied.
The patient tolerated the procedure well and left the department in stable
condition. There were no immediate complications.

The patient reported no change in the degree of  pain immediately following
the procedure.

COMPARISON:  MRI left hip ___.

FINDINGS: 

Fluoroscopic images demonstrated mild degenerative changes in the left hip. 
Injection of iodinated contrast confirmed needle tip positioning within joint
space.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  Findings - mild degenerative changes in the left hip.
2.  Procedure - Uneventful fluoroscopic-guided injection of0.25% Marcaine and
80 mg  Kenaloginto the left   hip  joint.

NOTIFICATION:  The procedure was supervised by Dr.  ___
, the attending radiologist, who was present for the critical portions of the
procedure.
